args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the latest deploy, checkout-api v2.3.1 was failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident.

- **What was wrong:** the latest deploy, v2.3.1, was failing health checks in us-east, us-west and eu-west, with an 18% error rate. Its test build, v2.3.1-rc, had also failed health checks in staging.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. All three regions now run v2.3.0, the service passes health checks, and the error rate is down to 0.2%.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open and has paged the on-call engineer. It describes the failure, the rollback and the current health, and says the cause of the v2.3.1 failure needs to be found before it's deployed again.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
